articles.title: When People Keep What Surgeons Remove
articles.summary: Emily likes her uterus much better in a jar than in her body. The 20-year-old, who asked to be identified by her first name to protect her privacy, keeps it in her bedroom, on what she calls her “dead things table,” among animal skulls and other specimens. After years of difficult symptoms, she had a hysterectomy at 19—and made arrangements to bring the organ home. articles.title: The Amputations America Can Prevent
articles.summary: I was born in Nigeria, and raised and educated in New Jersey and New York City. But more than a decade ago, my journey led me to the heart of the Mississippi Delta, a region whose rich history, resilience, hope, and deeply-rooted bloodlines tell a powerful American story. I arrived because I recognized an unmet healthcare need that could no longer be ignored—a disturbing pattern of preventable limb loss that I came to describe as the Black American amputation epidemic . articles.title: The Future of Libraries Is About More Than Books
articles.summary: In considering the role of libraries , I’m often pulled to the words of journalist, author, and longtime editor of Saturday Review , Norman Cousins. “The library is not a shrine for the worship of books,” he wrote in 1954. “It is not a temple where literary incense is burned or one’s devotion to the bound book is expressed in ritual.
